I am seventy-six years old now, so I cannot work the soil like I used to, but this plot has fed my family for generations. In Mbeya the rains are usually trustworthy, so I will plant the improved maize seed I kept from last season and put both manure and a little chemical fertilizer from the voucher program to keep the soil strong. My children and grandchildren will do most of the digging and weeding, but I will pay young men from the village for a few days to help with the heavy work of clearing and planting. I do not use sprays on maize—they cost too much—and there is no need for irrigation when the rains come.
